Fetch NJ high school cohort persistence

Source: R/fetch_stability.R
fetch_stability.Rd

Reads state-published high school persistence from bundled text extracts of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 School Performance Reports school databases. NJDOE defines it as the percentage of students in a graduation cohort who either graduated with a state-endorsed diploma or remained enrolled six years after entering high school. This is a cohort-persistence proxy, not annual same-school stability, mobility or fall-to-fall attrition. The definition is repeated in every row.

Usage

fetch_stability(end_year)

Arguments

end_year

Report school year end, 2024 or 2025.

Value

A tibble with end_year, entity_level, district_id, school_id, district_name, school_name, measure, student_group, value (percent), source_value, value_lo, value_hi, numerator, denominator, period, count_date, definition and source_file. Counts are unpublished and NA.

Details

The 2024-25 accountability release uses Cohort 2022 six-year data from 2023-24. It is distinct from the current-cohort persistence in the GraduationCohortProfile sheet. Groups with fewer than 10 students are unavailable; accountability calculations require at least 20 students. Published markers are retained in source_value. Specialized receiving schools are attributed to sending schools for accountability, per the SPR Reference Guide. No count or annual retention rate is inferred. The 2023-24 six-year profile names its measure HighSchoolPersistance; the 2024-25 profile names it Persisting. Those current-cohort rows are kept separately from HS Persistence accountability rows by measure and period.

Examples

x <- fetch_stability(2025)
subset(x, student_group == "Students with Disabilities")
